focus: Symlink-alias sweep: judge every path comparison under doctor scripts, .skilled/scripts and .skilled/bin for whether an alias path on one side makes it wrong; reproduce read-only.

label: path.resolve and fs.realpathSync both resolve an alias-terminated path lexically, so `.opencode/agents/..` yields `.opencode` from both and cannot detect the alias; divergence needs a descendant past the alias (`.opencode/agents/README.txt` gives `.opencode/agents/README.txt` vs `.skilled/agents/README.txt`). Any earlier finding that used an `..`-terminated alias path to prove sameness or difference is inconclusive and must be re-run with a descendant path.

The .opencode alias set is not uniform: agents, bin and scripts are git mode 120000 symlinks to ../.skilled/*, while .opencode/commands and .opencode itself are real directories. A symmetric alias sweep therefore reports .skilled/commands as a duplicate of separate content, and a sweep that de-duplicates by resolved path collapses two real trees.

worktree-status.sh strips MAIN_ROOT from each worktree path with no trailing separator, so a sibling checkout prints a non-existent path: MAIN_ROOT=/Users/dev/Skilled maps /Users/dev/Skilled-old/work/wt2 to `.-old/work/wt2`, and the guard comparing short_path to wt_path cannot fire because the strip did change the string. worktree-session.sh:248 does the same operation with an explicit separator.

symlink-engine.cjs answers the containment question twice: pointsIntoSource canonicalizes the longest existing prefix of the link text and compares on a segment boundary, while isHostRelativeLink uses a raw path.resolve against a canonical entrySource. The two disagree when a link text traverses a symlinked component that returns inside the source; no such link text exists in the mirror source today, so the finding is the missing guard in one of two siblings.

check-mcp-mutation-class.sh derives ROOT from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (physical) with a `pwd` (logical) fallback, then re-derives it with `cd` + `pwd` (logical again), so ROOT's physicality depends on which branch ran. The consumer `${path#"$ROOT"/}` at line 355 then degrades to printing full absolute paths when the manifest's declared paths are physical; no verdict flips because the existence test uses the absolute path directly. The Python block is canonical-safe because it applies os.path.realpath to both sides.

Eight further path comparisons audited and cleared: symlink-engine isWholeLink (realpath both sides), isAllowedGitExclude (both sides from the same canonical root), resolvesInto (realpath both sides), sk-skill-check, agents-md-manifest, opencode-version-battery's primary branch, git-setup-check's ctx.repoRoot, and the separator-bearing strips in pre-push and worktree-session.sh. Recorded so the next pass does not re-audit them; git-setup-check keeps `requested` and `repoRoot` as two spellings in one scope, safe only while nothing compares a hook link against `requested`.

Alias divergence reproduced three ways read-only: node path.resolve vs fs.realpathSync on a descendant path; shell cd+pwd -P vs git rev-parse --show-toplevel from a directory reached through an alias; and the ${x#"$root"} prefix strip with and without a trailing separator.

direction: Treat `.opencode/agents/..` as a cheap alias of `.skilled` for testing purposes
reason: Both path.resolve and fs.realpathSync cancel the `..` lexically and return `.opencode`, and bash cd does the same, so the form cannot demonstrate an alias at all.

direction: Claim isWholeLink's relative-link branch is a canonicalization bug
reason: Comparing literal link text to the manifest's declared target is the intended identity for a relative-link entry and cannot be satisfied by a resolved path; the finding there is uniformity of the alias set, not canonicalization.
